solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Party time for writer

parts.note: a ball is a formal dancing party
a point is a moment in time, as in 'at that point'

explanation.surface: Someone asks when the party for an author is being held.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro-style pen is a writing instrument, so 'writer' names it as the thing that writes.

clue.text: Artist's earnings brought home?

definitions.meaning: Francis ... was the British painter; the 's stands for 'is'
the idiom 'bring home the ...' means earn a living, so the ... is the earnings brought home

explanation.surface: A question about the money a painter takes back to the household.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the artist is the first sense; the question mark flags the idiom 'bring home the bacon', to earn the family's keep.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was a celebrated painter, and the idiom treats cured pork as a wage-earner's income.

clue.text: English town — Edinburgh a lot different, unknown couple claimed

indicators.note: claimed means the rearranged letters take in and hold the other piece
different says the letters of the Scottish capital, a and lot are made into something else

parts.note: taken as written
z is a mathematical unknown, so a couple of unknowns is ZZ

explanation.surface: A comparison of an English town with Edinburgh, mentioning a mysterious pair who staked a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges the fodder to LEIGHTONBUARD; 'claimed' takes the pair of algebraic unknowns in between U and A. Leighton Buzzard is a Bedfordshire market town.
explanation.definitionFit: Leighton Buzzard is a market town in Bedfordshire, England, so it is an example of an English town.

clue.text: Quick to arrest evil drug dealer

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold or seize, so the word for quick holds the word for evil inside it

parts.note: pacy means fast or quick
harm is injury or evil done

explanation.surface: Police urged to move fast and seize a wicked narcotics trafficker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug dealer' points to a criminal, but a chemist's shop legally deals in drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop dispenses and sells medicines, so it is a legitimate dealer in drugs.

clue.text: Entire town empty, strangely everyone communicating via this?

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put into an odd new order
empty means the inside of the word town is removed, keeping its outside letters

explanation.surface: A whole town deserted, oddly, while everyone is busy talking through some medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TN from town; 'strangely' rearranges ENTIRE plus TN.
explanation.definitionFit: The global computer network is how almost everybody now sends messages, the question mark hinting at that exaggeration.

clue.text: Duty bringing state to block river

indicators.note: to block is to obstruct, here by sitting inside the river's name

parts.note: the Taff is a river in South Wales, flowing through Cardiff
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A government levy imposed on account of a state damming a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is the river through Cardiff; RI (Rhode Island) blocks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax or duty charged on imported goods, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Country unable to take luggage back?

indicators.note: back says the phrase is read from end to start

parts.note: someone unable to take luggage has no bag

explanation.surface: A traveller's complaint that a nation will not let them bring their suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NO BAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a nation on the west coast of central Africa.

clue.text: One's chinned a supporter after game

indicators.note: after places the supporting piece behind the word for game

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
a tee supports the ball in golf

explanation.surface: Someone was punched on the jaw by a fan following a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chinned' looks like punched on the chin; read it as 'having a chin covering', so 'one's chinned' is what grows on the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed beard grows on the chin, so it is something with which one is 'chinned'.

clue.text: PC smashed gang raised in the city

indicators.note: smashed means one piece has broken into the gang, ending up inside it

parts.note: a band is a gang or group
PC, politically correct, means right-on
hove is an old past tense of heave, meaning raised

explanation.surface: A police constable broke up a gang that had grown up in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: PC is not the police officer but 'politically correct', i.e. right-on. Brighton and Hove is a seaside city on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton and Hove was granted city status in 2000, so it is the city meant.

clue.text: Blurred thing, then female's inferior vision so dreadful?

indicators.note: inferior means lower down, so in a down entry this piece sits below the first
blurred says the letters of thing lose their shape and are reformed

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A fuzzy object and a lesser woman make a frightening sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blurred' rearranges THING to NIGHT; 'inferior' means lower, so MARE goes under it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream is a frightening vision seen in sleep, hence a dreadful vision.

clue.text: Around margin, shift computer images

parts.note: c, short for circa, means around
a lip is an edge or margin
a shift is a trick or stratagem, and art can mean cunning artifice

explanation.surface: An instruction to move pictures on a screen round the edge of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' is not 'move' but an expedient or trick, which is one sense of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip art is ready-made graphics supplied for pasting into documents on a computer.

clue.text: University lesson

definitions.meaning: the University of ... is in Berkshire, England
a lesson is a passage of scripture read aloud in church

explanation.definitionFit: Reading is an English university town, and a lesson in church is a read passage.

clue.text: Prophet recalling an inarticulate sound

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, says the little word an is turned round

parts.note: a hum is a wordless sound

explanation.surface: A seer remembering a vague murmur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' turns AN into NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the Old Testament minor prophets, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Bullet finds soft tissue — scream about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for scream goes round the tissue

parts.note: a riot, like a scream, is something hilarious
flesh is the soft tissue of the body

explanation.surface: A wounding report: the round enters flesh and someone shrieks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scream' means a very funny thing, as does riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet fired from a rifle is a single discharge or shot of that gun.

clue.text: Time for inscription in delicate art, as mark scored

indicators.note: for inscription in means the letter is written into the craft's name

parts.note: crochet is the fine craft of hooked needlework

explanation.surface: An engraver writes on fine lacework, scratching a mark into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' is musical: a mark in a written score.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter note is a symbol written in a musical score, so it is a mark scored.

clue.text: Drink placed initially in drawer, short drink

parts.note: cha is tea, a drink

indicators.note: in means the first letter is put inside the shortened word
short says the word for drawer loses its last letter

parts.note: a magnet draws iron towards it, so it is a drawer

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of placed

explanation.surface: A beverage put in a cabinet, beside a small tot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' is not furniture but something that draws: a magnet, cut short to MAGNE. 'initially' gives P, put 'in' it after the M; CHA goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparkling French wine is a drink, so the definition is a broad category containing it.

clue.text: A little bit of a character, this Greek

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in 'not one jot'
the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A small part of a personality belonging to some Greek man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter's name has come to mean a very small amount, giving both senses.

clue.text: Japanese food I'm brought over, very very happy!

indicators.note: brought over, turned over in this down light, says I'm reads upwards

parts.note: I'm without the apostrophe gives IM
so means very, as in 'so kind'
so again means very
up means cheerful, as in 'feeling up'

explanation.surface: A delighted diner exclaims that a Japanese dish has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns IM into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso soup is a traditional Japanese broth of fermented soybean paste, so it is Japanese food.

clue.text: Too old to go topless, half of bits tucked away — too much said?

indicators.note: tucked away means put inside the shortened word
to go topless means losing the top letter, the first in this down light

parts.note: overage means too old

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of bits

explanation.surface: An aging person shouldn't strip off, with half their bits put away: is that saying too much?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' leaves VERAGE; 'half of' and 'tucked away' put the first two letters of bits inside it. The surface's nudity is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbiage is excessive wordiness, speech that uses far more words than needed.

clue.text: Macho man unable to open desk

indicators.note: unable to open says the name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Rambo is the film action hero, a byword for a macho man

explanation.surface: A tough guy can't get a desk open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unable to open' drops the R of RAMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised reading stand or pulpit in early churches, so a kind of desk.

clue.text: Dog given a draught to drink

parts.note: aired means exposed to a current of air, given a draught
ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: An animal is offered a swig of something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draught' looks like a drink, but here it is a current of air; the drink is ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so it is a type of dog.

clue.text: Slowing up, about to stop, straightened up?

indicators.note: about means round, so the reversed word goes round the other piece
up in a down light says the word is read upwards

parts.note: rit, ritardando, is the musical direction for slowing
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A vehicle slowing down and about to halt has been put back upright.
explanation.walkthrough: rit. (ritardando) is a musical direction; 'up' turns it to TIR and 'about' wraps it round the stop word. The question mark allows 'more straightened up' for the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater is the sense: a room more fully straightened up is tidier, a comparative of being neat.

clue.text: European issue throwing up a bit of light

parts.note: a mag, a magazine, comes out in issues

indicators.note: throwing up in a down light says the word reads upwards

parts.note: a ray is a thin beam, a bit of light

explanation.surface: A person from Europe has a problem that turns up a glimmer of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing up' turns RAY into YAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Magyar is a Hungarian, a member of the main ethnic group of Hungary in central Europe.

clue.text: Doughy dish with one cold filling, then last of roast duck to be plucked

indicators.note: filling means going inside the dish

parts.note: a pizza is a dish on a dough base
I is the Roman numeral one
C is cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of roast

parts.note: a duck is a zero in cricket, the shape of an O

explanation.surface: A menu of pizza with something cold inside, followed by roast duck ready for plucking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be plucked' is a musical direction: strings plucked, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizzicato is the instruction for strings to be plucked with the fingers instead of bowed.

clue.text: Stick with the ultimate in detergent as bathroom cleaner

parts.note: to bide is to stay put, to stick

indicators.note: the ultimate in picks the last letter of detergent

explanation.surface: Advice to stay loyal to the finest detergent for cleaning the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bathroom cleaner' suggests a product, but it is a fixture that cleans the user.
explanation.definitionFit: A low basin for washing oneself sits in the bathroom, so it is a cleaner found there.

clue.text: Meeting some way down Coventry Street

indicators.note: some way down says the letters lie partway along the words, read down this light

explanation.surface: A rendezvous somewhere along a street in Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a private meeting, especially an assignation between lovers.

clue.text: Juice is full of it-that's a downer

indicators.note: is full of means the meat juice holds the other word inside

parts.note: gravy is the juice from cooked meat

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a drink is full of something depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a downer' means something depressing, but here it is the force pulling everything down.
explanation.definitionFit: The force that pulls objects towards the earth is literally what brings things down.

clue.text: Precious thing, a politician's skill in speaking

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry, a precious thing
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A treasured asset: a politician's talent for public speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold; TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, eloquence before an audience.

clue.text: Plant — is one sage?

definitions.meaning: a shrub or small tree with white flowers and dark berries
a senior, wise member of a community or church

explanation.surface: Asking whether a herb is the one called sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb, which suits 'Plant', but here it means a wise person.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a common hedgerow shrub, and an elder is a senior respected for wisdom.

clue.text: Show that's on here

parts.note: re means on or concerning
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone points to a theatre performance that is running locally.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent is to depict or portray, which is one sense of show.
